title: Optionals: if let, guard let, and the force unwrap that crashes

videos.script: In many languages, any value can be missing, and nothing tells you which. The program finds out when it runs, usually in front of somebody. {{types}} Swift splits every type in two. String, which always holds a string. And String with a question mark, which may hold nothing at all. You will see the compiler refuse both mistakes before anything runs. {{iflet}} Then the four answers to one question: and if it is nil? If let, which checks and gives you a plain value inside the braces. {{guard}} Guard let, which leaves early and keeps the value for the rest of the function. {{coalesce}} The double question mark, which supplies a default. And the question-mark dot, which passes nil along a chain. {{bang}} And the exclamation mark, which gives the crash back. You will see that crash, and a printed line it swallowed. {{map}} Last, transforming a value without opening it. By the end, the planner reads durations a student typed, and knows what to do with the ones that are not numbers.
